items.title: Noah Cook Interview, 1960-08-30
items.q: And Miss Cartwright, she, oh, she had about, oh man, she must have had about seven or eight of children. Had a great big shed in the back. And a whole lot of desks, black boys. And she teached us from that.

ctx.x: Well, in those days, how long could they keep somebody? 24 hours.

Before they buried him. Yes, sir. No sister, you keep no weekend. No, you couldn't. If you died today, they buried you tomorrow. Out of that. Now, there's stuff that's stuff that's stinging you there and keep you in mind. But them days you didn't. If you died tonight, they buried you the next day. Yes, for them old men in the country and I was a boy and nobody died, they'd be getting out of their shovels and get down to the grave or dig that grave. And buried you. No, no keeping it. And then they'd preach funer…
You were a non-commissioned officer? Huh?
